newsitem.title: USA: Apple introduces small business Macintosh.
newsitem.headline: Apple introduces small business Macintosh.

text.p: In conjunction with its new and faster Power Macintosh 6500 and 4400 personal computer, Apple Computer Inc said it was unveiling the Apple Small Business Macintosh series of computers.
The configuration of the new 6500 and 4400 systems provided users with a comprehensive small business solution, the company said.

Initially, Apple said it would ship the Small Business Macintosh 6500/250 and the Small Business Macintosh 4400/200. The systems were bundled with industry-standard software and featured a built-in fax modem, 12x-speed CD-ROM drive, digital answering system and a speakerphone, it said.

"The Small Business Macintosh Series focuses on the needs of the small business market place and provides tailored solutions for this market," said Mike Muench, vice president of Apple's Consumer and Small Business division.

The Small Business Macintosh 6500/250 comes with a 250 MHz PowerPC 603e RISC processor with 256K level two cache, 48MB of RAM, 2MB video RAM, a 4GB hard disk and 1.4MB floppy disk drive, it said. The 4400/200 is based on a 200 MHz PowerPC 603e RISC processor with 256K level 2 cache, 32MB of RAM, 2MB video RAM, a 2GB hard disk and 1.4MB floppy disk drive.
The Apple Small Business Macintosh 6500/250 would be available at an estimated retail price of $2,599 and the 4400/200 at an estimated retail price of $1,999, the company said.
